# Unique-sector ears at a triangle saturating a Lorentz row

This note completes the previously untreated unique-tip parts of every
edge. It is a first-variation theorem for actual convex polygons. It
does not claim a uniform neighborhood theorem, an arbitrary-body Lorentz
inequality, or mixed-fiber compatibility.

## 1. Tight triangle and the differential of the selected row

Use source zero and normals (1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1). The complete positive
matrix equality characterization gives every strict-incidence triangle
tight at row 1, after interchanging labels 2 and 3 if needed, as

    P1=(2v+w,-v-w), P2=(-x,x+s), P3=(-x,-s-w),
    x,s,v>0, w>=0.

The parametrization and the actual triangle formulas are proved in
`candidate cfb017a0e12acfbf`.
Set

    p=2v+w, b=x+s, c=x+s+w, e=s+w,
    L=x+w+2v, B=x+2s+w, H=x+s+w+v,
    r=L/H, z^2=B/H, eta=4-r.

Here L+B=2H, B=b+e=c+s, 0<r<2, and eta=2+B/H. With k the area,
Q_i the raw cap areas and sigma_i their coarea chords, the exact data are

    k=LB/2,
    Q1=p^2 B/(2L), sigma1=pB/L,
    Q2=Lb^2/(2H), sigma2=Lb/H,
    Q3=Lc^2/(2H), sigma3=Lc/H.

For any nearby actual polygon put

    M=sum_i Q_i/sigma_i,
    F_i=2sqrt(k Q_i)/(sigma_i M),
    Phi1=F1+(F2+F3)^2/4.

At the stated triangle M=H, F1=r, F2=F3=z, and Phi1=2. Its differential
has the linear form

    Phi1'=c0 k'+sum_i c_i Q_i'+sum_i d_i sigma_i',       (1)

where, writing e1=r and e2=e3=z^2,

    c0=eta/(2k)=eta/(LB),
    c_i=e_i/(2Q_i)-eta/(H sigma_i),
    d_i=-e_i/sigma_i+eta Q_i/(H sigma_i^2).              (2)

These follow by differentiating F_i and using F2=F3 at the original
triangle. All the quantities being differentiated are positive.

**Lemma 1.** The constant area-density coefficient on each strict
unique-signature sector is positive:

    alpha_i:=c0+c_i>0.                                 (3)

**Proof.** For the other two vertices direct substitution gives

    alpha_2=[b^2+e^2-(B/H)be]/(LB b^2),
    alpha_3=[c^2+s^2-(B/H)cs]/(LB c^2).

They are positive because B/H<2 and all the displayed lengths are
positive. For vertex 1 put a=p/L in (0,1). Substitution and completion
of a square give

    alpha_1=[eta(a-r/2)^2+r(r-2)^2/4]/(LB a^2)>0.

The second summand in this numerator is strictly positive since
0<r<2. QED.

## 2. Actual ear derivatives as a linear tent functional

Consider any edge [P_j,P_k] and let P_l be the remaining vertex. Write

    P(t)=(1-t)P_j+tP_k,       0<=t<=1.

The j cap is positive on 0<=t<psi and the k cap on theta<t<=1, where

    0<theta<psi<1.                                      (4)

Indeed the l margin is strictly negative on the whole edge, while the
three margins sum to zero. Thus the j and k caps overlap on a nonempty
middle interval. The two remaining intervals are the unique j and
unique k portions of the edge.

Fix t in (0,1) and an outward vector w0 with
J=|det(P_k-P_j,w0)|>0. For sufficiently small epsilon>0 the actual
added set in

    conv(K, P(t)+epsilon w0)

is exactly the triangle over this edge. In the coordinates
P_j+s(P_k-P_j)+h w0, it has 0<=h<=epsilon T_t(s), where

    T_t(s)=s/t if s<=t, and (1-s)/(1-t) if s>=t.

This description is exact and the Jacobian is J. Consequently

    k'=J/2,
    Q_j'=J integral_0^psi T_t(s) ds,
    Q_k'=J integral_theta^1 T_t(s) ds,
    Q_l'=0.                                            (5)

Put Delta_j=v_j.(P_k-P_j) and similarly Delta_k. The coarea-section
derivatives are

    sigma_j'=J T_t(psi)/|Delta_j|,
    sigma_k'=J T_t(theta)/|Delta_k|,
    sigma_l'=0.                                        (6)

To justify (6) even when the peak equals a cut crossing, the cutting
line in these coordinates is s=s0-(v_i.w0)h/Delta_i. Its intersection
with the ear has h-length epsilon T_t(s0)+O(epsilon^2): T_t is continuous
and piecewise linear with bounded slopes for this fixed interior t.
The coarea Jacobian is J/|Delta_i|. Thus (6) is valid also at t=theta
or psi. It uses actual moving section geometry, not an interchange of
unproved volume derivatives. Formula (5) follows directly by integration
and dominated convergence; points on its threshold have zero area.

Equations (1), (5), and (6) express Phi1'/J as a linear functional
of T_t. Denote this functional by mathcal L.

## 3. The endpoint affine tents have zero cost

One has

    mathcal L(1-s)=mathcal L(s)=0.                       (7)

For example, at P_j move that vertex along the line of its OTHER
incident edge, away from P_l. The other incident supporting line stays
fixed, while the edge [P_j,P_k] sweeps an affine layer with profile
1-s, up to its positive area-Jacobian factor. This is an actual smooth
two-sided variation of triangles through the original triangle; strict
vertex incidences and source interior persist for small parameters of
either sign. The already proved triangle theorem gives Phi1<=2 for
both signs, with equality at parameter zero, so its derivative is zero.
This proves the first identity in (7); moving P_k proves the second.

This argument does not assume the varied triangles remain in the equality
family. A differentiable function attaining its two-sided local maximum
has zero derivative in the stated vertex-motion direction.

## 4. Complete unique-tip sign, on all three edges

**Theorem.** If an actual ear peak lies in a unique-signature portion of
any edge of the stated tight triangle, then Phi1'<0. The same strict
inequality holds at either adjacent boundary ray crossing. The limiting
affine endpoint profile has derivative zero.

**Proof.** If 0<t<=theta, all cut crossings lie at or after the peak.
Direct integration of T_t in (5) gives

    mathcal L(T_t)=alpha_j/2+E/(1-t),

where E is independent of t. In detail its terms are

    E=[-c_j(1-psi)^2+c_k(1-theta)^2]/2
       +d_j(1-psi)/|Delta_j|+d_k(1-theta)/|Delta_k|.

Taking t=0 gives the affine tent 1-s, whose functional is zero by
(7). Thus E=-alpha_j/2 and

    Phi1'=-J alpha_j t/[2(1-t)]<0.                      (8)

The equality case t=theta in this formula is allowed by (5)--(6).
Likewise if psi<=t<1, the same computation from the other endpoint
and mathcal L(s)=0 gives

    Phi1'=-J alpha_k(1-t)/(2t)<0.                        (9)

These formulas use the positive coefficients (3), so they hold for
every edge, including the two edges incident to the selected vertex.
At t=0 or t=1 their affine-profile values are zero by (7). QED.

For reference, on the vertical edge opposite P1, write the actual tip
as (-x-epsilon,t), so -e<t<b. In the upper unique part x<t<b, (8)--(9)
become the explicit formula

    Phi1'=(b-t)[(B/H)be-b^2-e^2]/[2Lb^2(e+t)]<0.

In the lower unique part -e<t<0 they become

    Phi1'=(e+t)[(B/H)sc-s^2-c^2]/[2Lc^2(b-t)]<0.

The respective ray-crossing endpoints t=x and t=0 are included. These
formulas come from the correct one-positive-vertex ear clipping; they
are not an extrapolation of the double-sector formula into a wrong
incidence regime.

## 5. What is and is not concluded at vertices and near them

For an outward point perturbation based exactly at an original vertex,
the visible added pieces have endpoint affine profiles on one or both
incident edges. Their costs vanish by (7), so the first derivative is
zero. This can also be checked by decomposing the added polygon into
the visible-edge triangles; they have disjoint interiors. Since all
three cap margins are nonzero at that vertex, the small common joining
segment meets none of the cutting lines, so no section contribution is
double counted.

Zero first derivative is not a finite-size sign certificate. Likewise
the strict derivative in (8) or (9) tends to zero as the peak tends to a
vertex. This note makes no uniform second-order claim in that regime.
Together with separately proved double-tip derivatives, it supplies
the full fixed-interior-peak first-variation check; a neighborhood
theorem would still have to control approaching-vertex peaks and the
relevant higher-order remainders.
